host.name: Host
host.short: A computer participating in a network.
host.def: A computer participating in a network. A host can run many processes and have several network interfaces.

process.name: Process
process.def: A running program. A server process must listen on an address and port to accept network connections.

client.name: Client
client.short: A program acting as the initiator of a request.
client.def: A program acting as the initiator of a request. The same program can be a client on one connection and a server on another.

server.name: Server
server.short: A program or machine providing a service to clients.
server.def: A program or machine providing a service to clients. Context tells you whether someone means the process, machine, or whole service.

packet.name: Packet
packet.short: A bounded unit of data carried by a network protocol, such as an IP packet.
packet.def: A bounded unit of data carried by a network protocol, such as an IP packet. An application message can span many packets.

frame.name: Frame
frame.short: A unit sent over a link-layer network, such as Ethernet.
frame.def: A unit sent over a link-layer network, such as Ethernet. A frame can carry an IP packet as its payload.

protocol.name: Protocol
protocol.short: An agreement about message formats and behavior between communicating participants, including what they send and how they respond.
protocol.def: An agreement about message formats and behavior between communicating participants, including what they send and how they respond.

encapsulation.name: Encapsulation
encapsulation.short: Wrapping higher-level data in a lower-level protocol’s headers or other framing.
encapsulation.def: Wrapping higher-level data in a lower-level protocol’s headers or other framing. Receivers interpret the layers in reverse order.

ip-address.name: IP address
ip-address.short: An Internet Protocol address used for delivery in a particular network context.
ip-address.def: An Internet Protocol address used for delivery in a particular network context. An address does not by itself identify a person or grant permission.

port.name: Port
port.short: A transport-level number that helps distinguish communication endpoints on a host.
port.def: A transport-level number that helps distinguish communication endpoints on a host. TCP port 443 and UDP port 443 are different protocol endpoints.

socket.name: Socket
socket.short: An operating-system communication endpoint used by a process.
socket.def: An operating-system communication endpoint used by a process. Network sockets are associated with protocols and addresses; not every socket uses IP.

loopback.name: Loopback
loopback.short: An interface for communication within the local network environment.
loopback.def: An interface for communication within the local network environment. 127.0.0.1 is an IPv4 loopback address; ::1 is its familiar IPv6 counterpart.

localhost.name: Localhost
localhost.def: A conventional hostname for loopback. Inside a container or Pod, its meaning follows that environment’s network namespace.

listener.name: Listener
listener.short: A server socket waiting for incoming connections on a bound address and port.
listener.def: A server socket waiting for incoming connections on a bound address and port. A running process may have no listener, or may listen only on loopback.

dns.name: DNS
dns.short: The Domain Name System: a distributed system for looking up records associated with names.
dns.def: The Domain Name System: a distributed system for looking up records associated with names. Resolving an address does not prove the application is reachable.

resolver.name: Resolver
resolver.def: Software that performs name lookups. A recursive DNS resolver can obtain answers from other DNS servers and cache them.

ttl.name: TTL
ttl.def: Time to live. In DNS, a cache lifetime for a record. In IP discussions, TTL refers to a different field limiting packet lifetime through hops; do not confuse the two.

cname.name: CNAME
cname.short: A DNS record that makes one name an alias for another canonical name.
cname.def: A DNS record that makes one name an alias for another canonical name. Resolving the alias can require additional lookups.

nxdomain.name: NXDOMAIN
nxdomain.short: A DNS response indicating that the queried name does not exist according to that response.
nxdomain.def: A DNS response indicating that the queried name does not exist according to that response. It is distinct from a resolver failing to answer.

cidr.name: CIDR
cidr.short: Classless Inter-Domain Routing notation represents an address prefix using an address and slash length.
cidr.def: Classless Inter-Domain Routing notation represents an address prefix using an address and slash length. In IPv4, /24 leaves eight bits for addresses in the range.

subnet.name: Subnet
subnet.short: An address range and associated network subdivision.
subnet.def: An address range and associated network subdivision. Provider rules determine which addresses can be assigned to resources.

route.name: Route
route.short: A forwarding rule connecting a destination prefix to a next hop or interface.
route.def: A forwarding rule connecting a destination prefix to a next hop or interface. A route alone does not prove permissions or a working return path.

router.name: Router
router.short: A device or system forwarding traffic between IP networks.
router.def: A device or system forwarding traffic between IP networks. Forwarding commonly uses the most specific matching destination prefix.

switch.name: Switch
switch.short: A device commonly used to forward frames within a link-layer network.
switch.def: A device commonly used to forward frames within a link-layer network. Modern hardware may also route IP traffic, so the exact role matters.

gateway.name: Gateway
gateway.short: A system connecting or mediating between environments.
gateway.def: A system connecting or mediating between environments. A default IP gateway forwards packets; an API gateway applies application-level policy. Ask which meaning is intended.

nat.name: NAT
nat.short: Network Address Translation: rewriting address information, often with port mappings so multiple private clients can share public IPv4 addresses.
nat.def: Network Address Translation: rewriting address information, often with port mappings so multiple private clients can share public IPv4 addresses.

ipv4.name: IPv4
ipv4.short: The widely used version of IP with 32-bit addresses, usually written as four decimal octets.
ipv4.def: The widely used version of IP with 32-bit addresses, usually written as four decimal octets. Private and public addressing have different routing contexts.

ipv6.name: IPv6
ipv6.short: The version of IP with 128-bit addresses.
ipv6.def: The version of IP with 128-bit addresses. A service can have IPv4 and IPv6 paths with different reachability.

arp.name: ARP
arp.short: Address Resolution Protocol: a mechanism for finding a local-link address for a directly reachable IPv4 destination, commonly the next-hop router.
arp.def: Address Resolution Protocol: a mechanism for finding a local-link address for a directly reachable IPv4 destination, commonly the next-hop router.

mtu.name: MTU
mtu.short: Maximum Transmission Unit: the largest network-layer packet size carried on a link without link-specific fragmentation.
mtu.def: Maximum Transmission Unit: the largest network-layer packet size carried on a link without link-specific fragmentation. Tunnels and other encapsulation can reduce the usable size.

tcp.name: TCP
tcp.short: Transmission Control Protocol: a transport that supplies an ordered, reliable byte stream while a connection is usable.
tcp.def: Transmission Control Protocol: a transport that supplies an ordered, reliable byte stream while a connection is usable. It does not guarantee application completion.

udp.name: UDP
udp.short: User Datagram Protocol: a transport for datagrams without built-in guarantees of delivery or order.
udp.def: User Datagram Protocol: a transport for datagrams without built-in guarantees of delivery or order. Higher-level protocols can add reliability over it.

quic.name: QUIC
quic.short: A secure transport over UDP that supplies streams and congestion control.
quic.def: A secure transport over UDP that supplies streams and congestion control. HTTP/3 uses QUIC instead of TCP.

handshake.name: Handshake
handshake.short: An exchange used to establish connection state or security parameters.
handshake.def: An exchange used to establish connection state or security parameters. TCP and TLS have different handshakes.

flow-control.name: Flow control
flow-control.short: Mechanisms preventing a sender from overwhelming the receiver’s available capacity.
flow-control.def: Mechanisms preventing a sender from overwhelming the receiver’s available capacity. In TCP this is distinct from protecting shared network capacity.

congestion-control.name: Congestion control
congestion-control.short: Mechanisms that adapt sending to shared network capacity.
congestion-control.def: Mechanisms that adapt sending to shared network capacity. They are different from application quotas such as requests per minute.

connection-pool.name: Connection pool
connection-pool.short: A finite set of reusable client connections.
connection-pool.def: A finite set of reusable client connections. Pool waiting and connection establishment are different contributors to elapsed time.

tls.name: TLS
tls.short: Transport Layer Security: a protocol providing protected communication and authentication mechanisms.
tls.def: Transport Layer Security: a protocol providing protected communication and authentication mechanisms. HTTPS normally validates the server’s identity through certificates.

https.name: HTTPS
https.short: HTTP using a secure transport with server authentication.
https.def: HTTP using a secure transport with server authentication. Successful HTTPS does not guarantee API authorization or a correct model answer.

certificate.name: Certificate
certificate.short: A signed statement binding identity information to a public key under a trust system.
certificate.def: A signed statement binding identity information to a public key under a trust system. Clients validate the chain, name, dates, and applicable rules.

sni.name: SNI
sni.short: Server Name Indication: TLS information identifying the hostname the client intends to contact, allowing servers to select appropriate configuration and certificates.
sni.def: Server Name Indication: TLS information identifying the hostname the client intends to contact, allowing servers to select appropriate configuration and certificates.

mtls.name: mTLS
mtls.short: Mutual TLS: TLS with certificate-based client authentication as well as server authentication.
mtls.def: Mutual TLS: TLS with certificate-based client authentication as well as server authentication. It is not automatically used by ordinary API-key-based HTTPS.

authentication.name: Authentication
authentication.def: Establishing an identity. TLS server identity and the client’s API identity are separate authentication questions.

authorization.name: Authorization
authorization.short: Deciding what an identified caller is permitted to do.
authorization.def: Deciding what an identified caller is permitted to do. A reachable service can still reject an authenticated request.

http.name: HTTP
http.short: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: application-level request/response semantics, including methods, fields, and status codes.
http.def: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: application-level request/response semantics, including methods, fields, and status codes. HTTP versions differ in framing and transport.

header.name: Header
header.short: A field carrying message metadata, such as Content-Type or Authorization.
header.def: A field carrying message metadata, such as Content-Type or Authorization. Some headers are sensitive and should be redacted from diagnostics.

api.name: API
api.short: Application Programming Interface: a contract for interacting with software.
api.def: Application Programming Interface: a contract for interacting with software. A network API adds application rules above its underlying protocols.

rpc.name: RPC
rpc.short: Remote Procedure Call: a style of invoking an operation on another process or machine.
rpc.def: Remote Procedure Call: a style of invoking an operation on another process or machine. Failures can leave uncertainty about whether remote work happened.

grpc.name: gRPC
grpc.short: An RPC framework commonly using HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers.
grpc.def: An RPC framework commonly using HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers. Its application status must be interpreted in addition to the HTTP exchange.

cors.name: CORS
cors.short: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: browser-enforced rules governing a page’s access to responses from other origins.
cors.def: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: browser-enforced rules governing a page’s access to responses from other origins. curl success does not establish browser permission.

sse.name: SSE
sse.short: Server-sent events: a text event-stream format commonly used for server-to-client streaming over HTTP.
sse.def: Server-sent events: a text event-stream format commonly used for server-to-client streaming over HTTP. Event framing and application completion are separate concerns.

websocket.name: WebSocket
websocket.short: A protocol for bidirectional messages over a persistent connection.
websocket.def: A protocol for bidirectional messages over a persistent connection. It differs from SSE and from raw TCP read boundaries.

ttft.name: Time to first token
ttft.short: Elapsed time until the client identifies the first generated content token or event under a stated measurement definition.
ttft.def: Elapsed time until the client identifies the first generated content token or event under a stated measurement definition. It is distinct from first byte and completion latency.

latency.name: Latency
latency.short: Elapsed time for a defined operation.
latency.def: Elapsed time for a defined operation. Always name the boundaries: connection setup, first token, completed response, or whole logical sample.

rtt.name: RTT
rtt.short: Round-trip time: elapsed time for a network exchange to go to a destination and back.
rtt.def: Round-trip time: elapsed time for a network exchange to go to a destination and back. It is not the same as total model response time.

bandwidth.name: Bandwidth
bandwidth.short: A capacity for carrying data, commonly measured in bits per second.
bandwidth.def: A capacity for carrying data, commonly measured in bits per second. It differs from achieved throughput and from latency.

throughput.name: Throughput
throughput.short: The achieved rate of useful work, such as completed samples per second.
throughput.def: The achieved rate of useful work, such as completed samples per second. Specify whether you count attempts, logical samples, bytes, or tokens.

percentile.name: Percentile
percentile.short: A value locating an observation within a distribution under a chosen convention.
percentile.def: A value locating an observation within a distribution under a chosen convention. Tail percentiles need enough observations and a clear failure-handling policy.

concurrency.name: Concurrency
concurrency.short: The number of operations active at the same time.
concurrency.def: The number of operations active at the same time. It is not a rate per minute and does not by itself enforce a provider quota.

rate-limit.name: Rate limit
rate-limit.short: A restriction on work over time, such as requests or tokens within a policy window.
rate-limit.def: A restriction on work over time, such as requests or tokens within a policy window. Limits can apply across many workers or clients.

backpressure.name: Backpressure
backpressure.short: Slowing or limiting upstream production when downstream capacity is constrained, so waiting and resource use stay bounded.
backpressure.def: Slowing or limiting upstream production when downstream capacity is constrained, so waiting and resource use stay bounded.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.short: A limit on a particular wait.
timeout.def: A limit on a particular wait. Library semantics vary; distinguish connection, pool, idle-read, and total-operation limits.

deadline.name: Deadline
deadline.short: A time budget or cutoff for an operation.
deadline.def: A time budget or cutoff for an operation. An end-to-end deadline must account for its included waits and retries.

retry.name: Retry
retry.short: Another attempt after an outcome that the policy deems retryable.
retry.def: Another attempt after an outcome that the policy deems retryable. It can duplicate work and should retain its own attempt identity.

idempotency.name: Idempotency
idempotency.short: The property that repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once.
idempotency.def: The property that repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once. It does not imply identical responses or zero additional cost.

jitter.name: Jitter
jitter.short: In retry policies, randomized delay that reduces synchronized retries.
jitter.def: In retry policies, randomized delay that reduces synchronized retries. In network performance discussions, it can instead mean variation in delay.

proxy.name: Proxy
proxy.short: An intermediary handling traffic on behalf of a caller or service.
proxy.def: An intermediary handling traffic on behalf of a caller or service. It can affect destinations, security boundaries, buffering, timing, and error responses.

load-balancer.name: Load balancer
load-balancer.short: A component distributing traffic across backends.
load-balancer.def: A component distributing traffic across backends. Its decision unit may be a connection or an application request, depending on its layer and implementation.

vpc.name: VPC
vpc.short: Virtual Private Cloud: AWS terminology for a configurable virtual network.
vpc.def: Virtual Private Cloud: AWS terminology for a configurable virtual network. It contains addressing and connectivity configuration, not automatic trust or encryption.

egress.name: Egress
egress.def: Traffic leaving an environment. An eval worker’s outbound model request is egress from the worker network.

ingress.name: Ingress
ingress.def: Traffic entering an environment. Kubernetes also uses Ingress as the name of an API object describing incoming HTTP routing.

security-group.name: Security group
security-group.short: In AWS, a stateful allow control associated with resources.
security-group.def: In AWS, a stateful allow control associated with resources. It is separate from route tables, network ACLs, and application authorization.

network-namespace.name: Network namespace
network-namespace.short: An isolated view of networking resources such as interfaces, routes, and sockets.
network-namespace.def: An isolated view of networking resources such as interfaces, routes, and sockets. Containers can have separate namespaces or deliberately share one.

container.name: Container
container.short: An isolated process environment using operating-system facilities.
container.def: An isolated process environment using operating-system facilities. Its networking depends on namespace and runtime configuration, not merely on its image.

pod.name: Pod
pod.short: A Kubernetes unit whose containers share networking and some other resources.
pod.def: A Kubernetes unit whose containers share networking and some other resources. localhost can connect containers in the same Pod, not arbitrary Pods.

service.name: Kubernetes Service
service.short: An abstraction for accessing a set of backends.
service.def: An abstraction for accessing a set of backends. A typical ClusterIP Service provides stable cluster-internal access, but other Service types and headless Services exist.

endpointslice.name: EndpointSlice
endpointslice.short: A Kubernetes object describing network endpoints associated with a Service.
endpointslice.def: A Kubernetes object describing network endpoints associated with a Service. Checking it helps distinguish a Service name from usable backend targets.

networkpolicy.name: NetworkPolicy
networkpolicy.short: A Kubernetes object constraining selected traffic flows when enforced by a supporting network plugin.
networkpolicy.def: A Kubernetes object constraining selected traffic flows when enforced by a supporting network plugin. Its presence alone does not prove enforcement.

region.name: Region
region.def: A provider-defined geographical deployment area. Different regions can imply different routes, latency, availability assumptions, and transfer costs.

availability-zone.name: Availability zone
availability-zone.short: A provider-defined isolated deployment location within a region.
availability-zone.def: A provider-defined isolated deployment location within a region. Specific failure and placement guarantees depend on the cloud provider.

nccl.name: NCCL
nccl.short: NVIDIA’s library for collective communication among GPUs.
nccl.def: NVIDIA’s library for collective communication among GPUs. Its internal traffic is distinct from the external HTTPS path to a model endpoint.

trace.name: Trace
trace.short: Related observations representing a request’s path through operations.
trace.def: Related observations representing a request’s path through operations. A distributed trace depends on instrumentation and propagated context.

span.name: Span
span.short: A timed operation within a trace, with identifiers and attributes that help relate it to other operations.
span.def: A timed operation within a trace, with identifiers and attributes that help relate it to other operations.

request-id.name: Request ID
request-id.short: An identifier supplied or propagated by a component for correlating a request with logs.
request-id.def: An identifier supplied or propagated by a component for correlating a request with logs. Different systems may use different IDs for the same logical sample.

attempt.name: Attempt
attempt.short: One execution of a request or operation.
attempt.def: One execution of a request or operation. Several attempts may belong to one logical evaluation sample.

circuit-breaker.name: Circuit breaker
circuit-breaker.short: A policy that temporarily stops calls to a failing dependency and controls recovery probes.
circuit-breaker.def: A policy that temporarily stops calls to a failing dependency and controls recovery probes. It is not a substitute for recording failed or unattempted work.

sandbox.name: Sandbox
sandbox.short: An environment that constrains code or tool execution.
sandbox.def: An environment that constrains code or tool execution. Its filesystem, identity, and network permissions are part of an agent evaluation’s task conditions.
